newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli parliament begins debate on Hebron deal.
newsitem.headline: Israeli parliament begins debate on Hebron deal.

text.p: Israel's parliament began a debate on Thursday on a deal with the PLO to hand over most of the West Bank town of Hebron to Palestinian rule.

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu opened the debate hours after his cabinet approved the deal. Israel said it would begin the Hebron redeployment only after parliament approves the handover in a vote later on Thursday.
"We are not leaving Hebron, we are redeploying in Hebron," Netanyahu said at the opening of a statement on the accord reached after months of intense negotiations.

Netanyahu, who unseated Shimon Peres in May 1996 elections, has refrained from implementing agreements the previous government signed with the Palestinians because of security concerns and other issues.

Netanyahu passed the accord in cabinet by a vote of 11-7, crushing a revolt by right-wing ministers opposed to handing to Arabs West Bank land they believe God promised Israel in the Bible. One cabinet minister resigned in protest.

The 120-seat parliament was expected to approve the deal by a wide margin in a vote that could begin late on Thursday. The Israeli army was already moving equipment out of Hebron but the official redeployment was to start after the vote.
